1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("Cr.P.C") has been filed by the petitioners praying for quashing of FIR bearing no. 262/2022 registered at Police Station Adarsh Nagar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC") and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Amit Ahlawat, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
5. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Prashant Kumar Mittal and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Vinay from Police Station Adarsh Nagar, Delhi.
6. The brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 18.01.2019 as per Hindu rites, customs and ceremonies.

It is stated that due to temperamental disputes, petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 started living separately since 06.09.2019 and as such on the complaint of complainant/respondent no.2, an FIR bearing no.
262/2022, Police Station Adarsh Nagar for the offence punishable under Section 498A/406/34 IPC Mohit Singla & Ors vs State (Nct Of Delhi) And Anr on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152742801/
1 was registered against the petitioners.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is further stated that matter has been amicably settled between petitioners and respondent no. 2 vide Memorandum of Understanding dated 12.11.2022.
7.

On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide Memorandum of Understanding dated 12.11.2022.
8.

It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family members.
9. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received third instalment of Rs. 10 lakh today i.e. 18.01.2023 through RTGS and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

10. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

11. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 262/2022 registered at Police Station Adarsh Nagar for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
12. The present petition stands disposed of.
13. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
